---
title: "Node Parameters"
---

This page documents the parameter patterns used across hosm_ros2_px4,
uav_control, and px4_offboard_lowlevel: how to declare and load them in C++,
how to structure the YAML files, how to support runtime updates, and how to
pass them from launch files without type errors.

---

## Declare → load pattern

Split parameter handling into two private methods: `declareParameters()` and
`loadParameters()`. Call both from the constructor, before any timer or
publisher is created.

```cpp
class ControllerNode : public rclcpp::Node {
public:
    ControllerNode() : Node("controller") {
        declareParameters();
        loadParameters();
        // timers, subscribers, publishers ...
    }

private:
    void declareParameters() {
        /* Physical model */
        declare_parameter("mass",    2.0);
        declare_parameter("gravity", 9.81);

        /* Nested gains use dotted names */
        declare_parameter("smc.lambda_z", 5.0);
        declare_parameter("smc.epsilon",  0.1);

        /* Control */
        declare_parameter("control_rate_hz", 250.0);
        declare_parameter("auto_arm",        true);
        declare_parameter("debug_thrust_only", false);

        /* Normalization */
        declare_parameter("max_thrust",       32.7);
        declare_parameter("max_torque_roll",   3.22);
    }

    void loadParameters() {
        params_.mass    = get_parameter("mass").as_double();
        params_.gravity = get_parameter("gravity").as_double();

        smc_.lambda_z = get_parameter("smc.lambda_z").as_double();
        smc_.epsilon  = get_parameter("smc.epsilon").as_double();

        control_rate_hz_  = get_parameter("control_rate_hz").as_double();
        auto_arm_         = get_parameter("auto_arm").as_bool();
        debug_thrust_only_ = get_parameter("debug_thrust_only").as_bool();

        max_thrust_      = get_parameter("max_thrust").as_double();
        max_torque_roll_ = get_parameter("max_torque_roll").as_double();
    }
};
```

::: {.callout-note}
Separating declare and load makes it easy to add `add_on_set_parameters_callback`
(see below) without scattering `declare_parameter` calls throughout the class.
:::

---

## YAML parameter file structure

ROS 2 parameter files follow `<node_name>: ros__parameters: <key>: <value>`.
Dotted C++ names (`smc.lambda_z`) expand into nested YAML maps.

```yaml
controller:
  ros__parameters:
    # physical model
    mass:    2.064
    gravity: 9.81

    # SMC gains — expressed as nested map matching the dotted C++ names
    smc:
      lambda_z:  5.0
      epsilon:   0.1

    # control
    control_rate_hz: 250.0
    auto_arm:        true
    debug_thrust_only: false

    # PX4 normalization (compute from motor characterization)
    max_thrust:      32.7
    max_torque_roll:  3.22
```

### Wildcard node name

Use `/**` to apply a block to every node in the process. Useful for shared
topic remapping conventions (e.g. FMU topic names) that should not need
repeating per-node:

```yaml
/**:
  ros__parameters:
    sitl_mode: true
    topics:
      odometry:  "/fmu/out/vehicle_odometry"
      status:    "/fmu/out/vehicle_status_v1"
```

---

## Dynamic parameter callback

Allow runtime parameter updates (e.g. gain tuning via `ros2 param set`) by
registering a callback in the constructor:

```cpp
ControllerNode() : Node("controller") {
    declareParameters();
    loadParameters();

    param_cb_handle_ = add_on_set_parameters_callback(
        [this](const std::vector<rclcpp::Parameter>& params) {
            return onParameterChange(params);
        });
}

rcl_interfaces::msg::SetParametersResult
onParameterChange(const std::vector<rclcpp::Parameter>& params) {
    rcl_interfaces::msg::SetParametersResult result;
    result.successful = true;

    for (const auto& p : params) {
        if (p.get_name() == "smc.lambda_z") {
            smc_.lambda_z = p.as_double();
            RCLCPP_INFO(get_logger(), "smc.lambda_z -> %.3f", smc_.lambda_z);
        } else if (p.get_name() == "auto_arm") {
            auto_arm_ = p.as_bool();
        } else if (p.get_name() == "debug_thrust_only") {
            debug_thrust_only_ = p.as_bool();
        }
    }
    return result;
}

rclcpp::node_interfaces::OnSetParametersCallbackHandle::SharedPtr param_cb_handle_;
```

Then at runtime:

```bash
ros2 param set /controller smc.lambda_z 8.0
ros2 param set /controller debug_thrust_only true
```

## Loading parameters from a launch file

### Layer YAML + runtime overrides

Pass the YAML file as the first entry in `parameters=[]` and add a dict of
runtime values afterwards. Later entries override earlier ones:

```python
Node(
    package="my_pkg",
    executable="controller_node",
    name="controller",
    output="screen",
    parameters=[
        LaunchConfiguration("params_file"),          # YAML file
        {
            "use_sim_time":   LaunchConfiguration("use_sim_time"),
            "auto_arm":       LaunchConfiguration("auto_arm"),
        },
    ],
)
```

### ParameterValue type casting

Launch configuration values are always strings. Without explicit casting,
float and int parameters arrive at the node as strings and cause a
`ParameterTypeMismatch` error at runtime:

```python
from launch_ros.parameter_descriptions import ParameterValue
from launch.substitutions import LaunchConfiguration

Node(
    package="my_pkg",
    executable="reference_publisher",
    parameters=[{
        "height":  ParameterValue(LaunchConfiguration("z"),     value_type=float),
        "speed":   ParameterValue(LaunchConfiguration("speed"), value_type=float),
        "samples": ParameterValue(LaunchConfiguration("n"),     value_type=int),
    }],
)
```

Use `ParameterValue` whenever a node expects a non-string parameter that comes
directly from a `LaunchConfiguration` rather than a Python literal.

---

## Dumping and inspecting parameters at runtime

```bash
# List all parameters for a node
ros2 param list /controller

# Get one value
ros2 param get /controller smc.lambda_z

# Dump all to YAML (useful for capturing a tuned config)
ros2 param dump /controller > tuned_params.yaml

# Load a file into a running node
ros2 param load /controller /path/to/tuned_params.yaml
```
